name: CSRB

summary.text: The Cyber Safety Review Board (CSRB) was a Department of Homeland Security review body, chaired by DHS Under Secretary Robert Silvers, that examined major cyber incidents. Its report on the 2023 Microsoft Exchange Online intrusion by the China-linked actor Storm-0558, dated March 20, 2024 and released April 2, 2024, found the intrusion was preventable and resulted from a 'cascade of security failures' at Microsoft, and judged the company's security culture 'inadequate'.

facts.claim: The Board found that Microsoft's security culture was inadequate and required an overhaul, attributing a set of decisions to a corporate culture that deprioritised enterprise security investments and rigorous risk management.

openQuestions: The site's phrases 'a cascade of security failures' and 'inadequate' security culture are supported by press accounts of the report. The report itself on cisa.gov/dhs.gov was not reachable; the owner should cite it directly.

The site labels the body 'CISA Cyber Safety Review Board'. Press coverage describes the CSRB as a DHS body distinct from CISA (CISA provided its secretariat). The two site ids csrb and cisa-cyber-safety-review-board refer to the same organisation and could be merged.
Sources differ on whether 22 or 25 organisations' email accounts were affected by Storm-0558.
